title.narrative: COVID-19: Second Shock-Responsive Social Protection Project

description.narrative: With a worsening coronavirus disease (COVID-19) situation unfolding in the fourth quarter of 2020, the Government of Mongolia has requested urgent additional support for social protection measures to mitigate the socioeconomic impacts of the pandemic on poor and vulnerable groups. The proposed project will (i) apply shock-responsive social protection principles to continue support for pro-poor child grant top-ups on a temporary basis through an established national social assistance program, and (ii) strengthen social welfare programs and systems for improved household resilience and government response to future crises.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President
Reports and Recommendations of the President
Loan 4051: 100% of contracts awarded and 100% disbursed as of 23 Apr 2025
Loan 4052: 96% of contracts awarded and 96% disbursed as of 23 Apr 2025

Progress Toward Outcome: Loan 4051-MON(COL) was financially closed on 1 Nov 2022, with almost 100% contract award and disbursement. For Loan 4052-MON(OCR), ADB approved the loan extension until 31 August 2024, reallocation of loan proceeds, changes to the design and monitoring framework, and revisions to the procurement plan. Three missions were conducted: loan inception mission on 30 Sep-13 Oct 2021 (virtual, intermittent); loan review mission on 22 Jun-1 Jul 2022 (virtual, intermittent); and midterm review mission on 27 Feb-3 Mar 2023. ADB approved in Nov 2021 a minor change in scope to cover CMP payments from July to December 2021, as requested by MOF. The procurement plan has been revised as follows: (i) cancel goods package G002 and consulting services package C009 and combine both of them under a new consulting services package C010 to engage an NGO using limited competitive bidding to implement the graduation pilot program, (ii) cancel goods packages G003 and G004, (iii) change the procurement method for G001 (Oracle database) from direct contracting to open competitive bidding, and (iv) minor changes to estimated values and advertisement dates for most of the packages. G001 was awarded on 21 October 2022 and completed on 15 Feb 2023. Two consulting firms were mobilized (C010 for the implementation of the graduation pilot program and C013 for market assessment), the remaining one (C014 for media services) is in the RFP issuance stage. Of the 11 individual consultants, 10 were engaged and the EA requested to cancel the remaining one.
Some results are in the Audited Project Financial Statements | Jul 2024: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/54214/54214-002-apfs-en_1.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: Output 1 has been completed and the target was exceeded. The project supported 7 months of topped-up child grant benefits (January to June and December 2021). The total number of children increased from 1,190,283 in January to 1,208,411 in June and 1,220,158 in December 2022. On average, girls comprised 48.9% of the total.
Output 2 is on track and in progress. Capacity building activities that were completed include business idea training (Mar/Apr 2023), training for survey data collectors (May 2023), training for enumerators (May 2023), business skills training (June 2023), technical skills training (July 2023), and savings group training. The proxy means test survey to re-certify 26,900 households started in May 2023. The connection with the databases of other public institutions such as General Taxation Office, GAHSI, and GOLWS is underway. The consulting firm for the graduation pilot program started the procurement of assets for the beneficiaries.
